name: toolsmith-json-set
intent: Set one value in a JSON file, keeping its existing layout.
use_when: You change, add or append one value in a JSON file such as settings.json, package.json or a manifest.
You would otherwise write a jq, Python or Ruby script that loads the JSON, changes a key and dumps it back.
not_for: YAML, TOML or JSON with comments (JSONC): those are not JSON.
Deleting keys, or several changes at once: run it once per change, or edit the file.
Reading values: use jq or the Read tool.
input: Three arguments. The file. The path: keys joined by '.', array items as [N] (from 0), [] at the end to append to an array, and "double quotes" around a key that holds '.', '[' or '"' (for example '"a.b".c'). The value: JSON, so a string needs its quotes ('"text"'); with --string the value is taken as a plain string. Missing objects on the path are created, and a missing array before []; a missing array before [N] is an error.

options.text: Take the value as a plain string, without JSON quotes.

output: '<file>: <path> = <value>', with '(was <old value>)' when a value was replaced; 'already <value>; file unchanged' when it was already set. Only the changed value's text is rewritten, or the new member's text added beside its neighbours with their separator and indent; every other byte of the file stays as it was. The file is written through a temporary file and a rename. If the change cannot be made in place, the whole file is written in the standard pretty style (key order, indent and final newline kept) and a note says so.

exit_codes.text: The value is set (or already was).
Nothing written: the file is missing or not valid JSON, or the path does not fit the data.
Nothing written: the path, the value or the arguments are wrong.

examples.title: Bump a version; the inline object and array stay on one line
Replace a value with a plain string
A path that does not fit the data
examples.stderr: toolsmith-json-set: package.json: name: is a string, so it has no key "first"

examples.title: A string value without its JSON quotes
examples.stderr:
toolsmith-json-set: the value store is not JSON; quote a string as '"text"', or add --string
Run `toolsmith-json-set --help` for usage, or `toolsmith-json-set --llm` for the full guide.
